item.title: America’s Labor Market Is Paralyzed by Policy and Economic Uncertainty
item.description: In markets, options to buy and sell securities get more valuable when volatility increases. The same is true of employers making hiring and firing decisions in times of surging input costs like energy prices, chaotic trade policies and transformative technologies. When you can’t predict next quarter’s bottom line, you’re better off retaining optionality, delaying staffing decisions that can involve steep up-front costs and are difficult to reverse. item.title: The Tech Mogul Strongman Is On the Rise
item.description: The rise of the liberal order in the 19th century depended on two revolutions. The most obvious was in the political sphere, where reformers restrained over-mighty rulers with a combination of constitutional rules and individual rights. But just as important was the transformation of the business world that created public companies, answerable to their shareowners rather than the government.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Hegseth Is Gutting the Army Amid War With Iran
item.description: The sudden departure of Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, following months of tension with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, is a serious blow to American security. Worse, his resignation follows the forcing out of several top Army generals, including Chief of Staff Randy George, Vice Chief James Mingus and the highly regarded combat commander of US Army Europe, Chris Donahue.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis
